title: Q-CTRL Achieves RTCA DO-160 Airworthiness Qualification for Ironstone Opal Quantum Navigation - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Q-CTRL's Ironstone Opal quantum magnetic navigation system achieved RTCA DO-160 safety-of-flight qualification, which the source calls the first quantum navigation payload certified for commercial aerospace and UAVs; it meets RNP 0.3 accuracy without satellites, is ITAR-free and comes in a sub-1 kg UAV variant amid GPS jamming affecting over 1,500 flights daily.

insights.claim: Q-CTRL's Ironstone Opal quantum magnetic navigation system achieved safety-of-flight qualification under the RTCA DO-160 environmental testing standard, described as the first quantum navigation payload certified for commercial aerospace and UAV deployment.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Certification moves quantum sensing from R&D into procurable aviation hardware, an early revenue path outside computing.
insights.quote: the first quantum navigation payload certified for commercial aerospace and uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) deployment
insights.locator: Quantum infrastructure and sensing company Q-CTRL

insights.claim: Ironstone Opal meets RNP 0.3 navigation accuracy (under 0.3 nautical miles over 95% of flight) without satellite signals.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Meeting civil-aviation accuracy thresholds makes it a credible GPS backup for airlines.
insights.locator: Q-CTRL Ironstone Opal Operational & Certification Benchmarks

insights.claim: Ironstone Opal comes in a crewed aviation unit and a sub-1 kg UAV module for NATO Class II+ drones, and is ITAR-free, allowing international commercial and allied defense deployment without U.S. munitions restrictions.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: ITAR-free status widens the export market, a meaningful commercial edge in defense sales.
insights.locator: Q-CTRL Ironstone Opal Operational & Certification Benchmarks

insights.claim: GPS jamming and spoofing disrupt more than 1,500 commercial flights daily, pushing aviation regulators and defense agencies to seek passive alternatives to satellite positioning.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Electronic warfare's spillover into civil aviation creates urgent, regulator-driven demand for alt-PNT.
insights.quote: disrupting more than 1,500 commercial flights daily
insights.locator: Rising global incidents of GPS jamming

insights.claim: Unlike inertial navigation that accumulates drift, Ironstone Opal uses atomic quantum sensors to measure variations in Earth's crustal magnetic field and matches them to onboard geomagnetic maps, with AI software filtering airframe interference in real time.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Passive, non-emitting operation is stealth-friendly and unjammable, fitting military as well as civil needs.

insights.claim: Ironstone Opal has undergone flight evaluations with Airbus, Lockheed Martin and U.S. defense programs, with live demonstrations planned at the Farnborough International Airshow.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Tier-1 aerospace partners are validating the product, signaling potential procurement contracts.
insights.locator: To operate reliably inside magnetically noisy

insights.claim: Q-CTRL has a $24.4 million DARPA Robust Quantum Sensors (RoQS) award.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Defense funding underwrites Q-CTRL's sensing business alongside its software lines.
